modules.title: Lead Scoring
modules.description: Weighted scoring across company size, budget, decision-maker status, engagement, and timeline. Automatic disqualification for competitors and students. Hot/warm/cold tier derivation with configurable thresholds.

inputs.name: company_size
inputs.note: Company size: enterprise or mid_market score points; any other size (smb) scores nothing.

inputs.name: engagement
inputs.note: Engagement level: high or medium score points; low or absent scores nothing.

inputs.name: budget_confirmed
inputs.note: true scores budget_points; false disqualifies the lead (no_budget); absent does neither.

inputs.name: decision_maker
inputs.note: true when the contact can sign; scores decision_maker_points.

inputs.name: timeline
inputs.note: Quarter the lead expects to buy in: q1 or q2 score points; later or unknown scores nothing.

inputs.name: competitor
inputs.note: true when the lead works for a competitor; disqualifies it.

inputs.name: student
inputs.note: true when the lead is a student; disqualifies it.

inputs.name: enterprise_points
inputs.note: Points for an enterprise company.

inputs.name: mid_market_points
inputs.note: Points for a mid-market company.

inputs.name: budget_points
inputs.note: Points for a confirmed budget.

inputs.name: decision_maker_points
inputs.note: Points for a decision maker.

inputs.name: high_engagement_points
inputs.note: Points for high engagement.

inputs.name: med_engagement_points
inputs.note: Points for medium engagement.

inputs.name: q1_timeline_points
inputs.note: Points for a q1 timeline.

inputs.name: q2_timeline_points
inputs.note: Points for a q2 timeline.

inputs.name: qualified_threshold
inputs.note: Score at or above which a lead that is not disqualified is qualified.

inputs.name: hot_threshold
inputs.note: Score at or above which a lead is hot.

inputs.name: warm_threshold
inputs.note: Score at or above which a lead is warm; below it the lead is cold.

modules.title: Invoice Rules
modules.description: Overdue detection, days-overdue calculation, late fee computation (flat or percentage with cap), escalation levels (reminder/warning/collections), and total amount due.

inputs.name: due_absolute_days
inputs.note: Due date as a day count from 1970-01-01. Preferred over the parts.

inputs.name: due_year
inputs.note: Due date in parts, with due_month and due_day, when due_absolute_days is absent.

inputs.name: due_month
inputs.note: Due month, 1 to 12.

inputs.name: due_day
inputs.note: Due day of the month.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.note: The amount owed: the base for the late fee and the amount now due.

inputs.name: paid
inputs.note: true once paid; a paid invoice is never overdue.

inputs.name: absolute_days
inputs.note: Today as a day count from 1970-01-01, the shared convention.

inputs.name: year
inputs.note: Today in parts, with month and day, when absolute_days is absent.

inputs.name: month
inputs.note: The month of today.

inputs.name: day
inputs.note: The day of the month of today.

inputs.name: late_fee_flat
inputs.note: Flat late fee, used when no late_fee_pct is set.

inputs.name: late_fee_pct
inputs.note: Late fee as a fraction of the amount (0.015 is 1.5%); wins over the flat fee.

inputs.name: late_fee_cap
inputs.note: Largest late fee charged.

inputs.name: warning_days
inputs.note: Days overdue at which the escalation level becomes warning.

inputs.name: collections_days
inputs.note: Days overdue at which the escalation level becomes collections.

modules.title: Approval Chains
modules.description: Multi-step approval workflows with delegation, rejection tracking, and automatic amount-based approver escalation. Finds next pending approver, checks full approval, and surfaces blocking reasons.

inputs.name: request
inputs.note: The request this step belongs to.

inputs.name: approver
inputs.note: Who must approve at this step.

inputs.name: step
inputs.note: Position in the chain; steps are approved in ascending order.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.note: Amount above which every request also needs this rule's approver, after the numbered steps.

inputs.name: approver
inputs.note: Who must approve a request whose amount exceeds the threshold.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.note: Amount compared against every threshold rule; without one no rule applies.

inputs.name: approved_by
inputs.note: An approver (or their delegate) who has approved the request.

inputs.name: rejected_by
inputs.note: An approver who rejected the request; any rejection stops the chain.

inputs.name: rejection_reason
inputs.note: Why the request was rejected, returned by approval_blocked.

inputs.name: delegated_to
inputs.note: Someone whose approval counts as this approver's.

modules.title: Inventory Management
modules.description: Stock level classification (adequate/low/critical/stockout), reorder triggers, order quantity calculation, preferred supplier selection, and days-of-stock forecasting.

inputs.name: stock
inputs.note: Units on hand, decimals allowed; 0 or less is a stockout.

inputs.name: supplied_by
inputs.note: A supplier of the item; with several, a preferred one is chosen first.

inputs.name: reorder_threshold
inputs.note: Stock at or below which the item is low and needs reordering.

inputs.name: critical_threshold
inputs.note: Stock at or below which the item is critical; default half the reorder_threshold, or 5 without one.

inputs.name: reorder_quantity
inputs.note: Units to order; default max_stock less stock, or 50 without a max_stock.

inputs.name: max_stock
inputs.note: Shelf capacity, used to size an order when no reorder_quantity is set.

inputs.name: daily_usage
inputs.note: Units used per day; without it, or at 0, days_of_stock is unknown.

inputs.name: preferred
inputs.note: true marks the supplier preferred_supplier returns ahead of the item's others.

modules.title: Pricing Rules
modules.description: Customer tier pricing, percentage and flat discounts, tier-gated discounts, bulk quantity breaks, floor/ceiling clamping, and final effective price calculation.

inputs.name: base_price
inputs.note: List price, before the tier multiplier and discounts.

inputs.name: has_discount
inputs.note: A discount rule that applies to this item; several add up.

inputs.name: price_floor
inputs.note: Lowest price price_capped returns.

inputs.name: price_ceil
inputs.note: Highest price price_capped returns.

inputs.name: pct_off
inputs.note: Percent of the base price (20 is 20%) taken off the tier price, so it adds to the tier multiplier rather than compounding (member 0.9 with 20 off 100 pays 70); wins over flat_off.

inputs.name: flat_off
inputs.note: Flat amount off, used when the discount has no pct_off.

inputs.name: requires_tier
inputs.note: Tier a customer must be on for effective_price to apply this discount; absent applies to everyone.

inputs.name: pricing_tier
inputs.note: The customer's pricing tier; a customer without one is standard.

inputs.name: member_multiplier
inputs.note: Multiplier on the base price for members (0.9 is 10% off).

inputs.name: vip_multiplier
inputs.note: Multiplier on the base price for VIPs (0.8 is 20% off).

modules.title: Loyalty Program
modules.description: Lifetime points accumulation, tier derivation (bronze/silver/gold/platinum), reduced redemption costs at higher tiers, reward eligibility, and inherited tier benefits.

inputs.name: lifetime_points
inputs.note: Points ever earned: sets the tier and is the base of the balance.

inputs.name: redeemed_points
inputs.note: Points ever redeemed, subtracted from lifetime_points for the balance.

inputs.name: points_cost
inputs.note: Points the reward costs before the tier's redemption multiplier.

inputs.name: has_benefit
inputs.note: A benefit granted at this tier (platinum, gold, silver or bronze) and every tier above it.

inputs.name: benefit_value
inputs.note: What tier_benefit returns for this benefit, as given (true, or a level such as priority).

inputs.name: platinum_threshold
inputs.note: Lifetime points at which a customer is platinum.

inputs.name: gold_threshold
inputs.note: Lifetime points at which a customer is gold.

inputs.name: silver_threshold
inputs.note: Lifetime points at which a customer is silver; below it the customer is bronze.

inputs.name: platinum_redemption_multiplier
inputs.note: Multiplier on a reward's points cost for platinum customers (0.7 is 30% fewer points).

inputs.name: gold_redemption_multiplier
inputs.note: Multiplier on a reward's points cost for gold customers.

inputs.name: silver_redemption_multiplier
inputs.note: Multiplier on a reward's points cost for silver customers; bronze always pays 1.0.

modules.title: Scheduling
modules.description: Time slot availability, booking conflict detection, advance window enforcement, role-gated booking prerequisites, and resource utilization percentage.

inputs.name: slots
inputs.note: Every bookable slot on the resource, e.g. [9,10,11,13]; utilisation is booked slots over its length.

inputs.name: booked_at
inputs.note: One existing booking on the resource; it blocks its slot on its date.

inputs.name: advance_days
inputs.note: Fewest days ahead of today a booking may be made.

inputs.name: max_advance
inputs.note: Most days ahead of today a booking may be made; also how far next_available_slot searches.

inputs.name: requires_role
inputs.note: When set, only a customer with this role can book the resource.

inputs.name: slot
inputs.note: The slot the booking holds, one of its resource's slots.

inputs.name: date
inputs.note: The day the booking is for.

inputs.name: role
inputs.note: The customer's role, matched against a resource's requires_role.

inputs.name: absolute_days
inputs.note: Today as a day count from 1970-01-01, the shared convention. Preferred over date.

inputs.name: date
inputs.note: Today as a day count, a YYYYMMDD integer or an ISO atom, when absolute_days is absent.

modules.title: Duty
modules.description: Duty conflicts, unavailability windows (leave, maintenance), maximum duty length, minimum rest, rolling cumulative limits, qualification currency, and role gating for people and the equipment they use. Ask whether a proposed duty is clean, who is available for it, and exactly why someone is not.

inputs.name: role
inputs.note: The worker's role; having one puts the worker on the roster available_staff searches.

inputs.name: duty_period
inputs.note: A committed duty period, past, current or scheduled; conflicts, rest and rolling totals come from these.

inputs.name: unavailable_during
inputs.note: Leave, training or maintenance; any entity can carry it, equipment included.

inputs.name: holds
inputs.note: A qualification the worker holds.

inputs.name: max_duty
inputs.note: This worker's longest single duty period, in the namespace's time unit; overrides role and duty_policy.

inputs.name: min_rest
inputs.note: This worker's least rest between a prior duty's end and a new start; overrides role and duty_policy.

inputs.name: rolling_window
inputs.note: This worker's window for rolling_limit, ending at the proposed end; overrides role and duty_policy.

inputs.name: rolling_limit
inputs.note: This worker's most duty time within a rolling_window; overrides role and duty_policy.

inputs.name: max_duty
inputs.note: Longest single duty period for workers in this role, in the namespace's time unit.

inputs.name: min_rest
inputs.note: Least rest before a new start for workers in this role.

inputs.name: rolling_window
inputs.note: Window over which rolling_limit is measured for workers in this role.

inputs.name: rolling_limit
inputs.note: Most duty time within a rolling_window for workers in this role; enforced only with a window.

inputs.name: max_duty
inputs.note: Longest single duty period when neither worker nor role sets one; unset means unlimited.

inputs.name: min_rest
inputs.note: Least rest before a new start when neither worker nor role sets one; unset means none.

inputs.name: rolling_window
inputs.note: Window for rolling_limit when neither worker nor role sets one.

inputs.name: rolling_limit
inputs.note: Most duty time within a rolling_window when neither worker nor role sets one; unset means unlimited.

inputs.name: start
inputs.note: When the duty period starts, included, in the namespace's time unit.

inputs.name: end
inputs.note: When the duty period ends, excluded: a period ending at 1080 and one starting at 1080 do not overlap.

inputs.name: start
inputs.note: When the unavailability starts, included, in the namespace's time unit.

inputs.name: end
inputs.note: When the unavailability ends, excluded.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.note: What the qualification certifies, matched against a task's requires.

inputs.name: expires
inputs.note: When it lapses, in the namespace's time unit; current while expires is later than the time asked about. Absent never lapses.

inputs.name: requires
inputs.note: A qualification kind the task needs, current at the duty's start; zero or more per task.

inputs.name: needs_role
inputs.note: The role a worker must have to take the task; absent accepts any role.

modules.title: Rostering
modules.description: Roster coverage, violations, candidate ranking, greedy fill, replacements, swaps, and load balance over the duty battery, plus an assign-battery model for exact fill of open seats. Proposals come back as terms to assert; nothing is written.

inputs.name: needs
inputs.note: One seat requirement of the shift, one per role needed.

inputs.name: start
inputs.note: When the shift starts, included, on the duty battery's timeline and in its time unit.

inputs.name: end
inputs.note: When the shift ends, excluded, in the same unit as start.

inputs.name: assigned
inputs.note: A worker currently on the shift; coverage, violations, load and swaps are computed from these.

inputs.name: seat
inputs.note: The role this seat requirement is for, matched against a worker's role.

inputs.name: count
inputs.note: How many workers with that role the shift needs.

inputs.name: role
inputs.note: The worker's role; only workers whose role matches a seat are candidates for it.

inputs.name: prefers
inputs.note: A shift the worker would like; ranks the worker first for it.

inputs.name: avoids
inputs.note: A shift the worker would rather not take; ranks the worker last for it.

inputs.name: seniority
inputs.note: Last ranking key; higher ranks earlier.

modules.title: Compliance
modules.description: Policy compliance checks, violation surfacing by requirement, data retention window validation, consent type mapping to actions, and consent registry queries.

inputs.name: requires
inputs.note: A requirement of the policy; an entity meets it with an attribute of that name whose value is not false, none or missing.

inputs.name: retention_days
inputs.note: Oldest a record may be, in days, under this policy; seven years when absent.

inputs.name: created_day
inputs.note: The day the record was created; its age is today minus this.

inputs.name: absolute_days
inputs.note: Today as a day count from 1970-01-01, the shared convention. Preferred over date.

inputs.name: date
inputs.note: Today as a day count, a YYYYMMDD integer or an ISO atom, when absolute_days is absent.

inputs.name: requires_consent
inputs.note: The consent type that must be held before the action is performed.

inputs.name: granted_consent
inputs.note: A consent type the customer has granted.

modules.title: BOM Policy
modules.description: Bill-of-materials policy over part-intelligence facts: lifecycle stage, end-of-life and last-time-buy dates, source count, compliance and qualification flags, declared alternates. Which parts block a build, which are due for a last-time buy, which alternate is usable; thresholds as facts, waivers as a hook.

probes.goal: findall(R, bom_violation(board, auto, cap_x, R), Rs)
findall(P-D, last_time_buy_due(board, auto, P, D), Due)

inputs.name: includes
inputs.note: One part on the bill of materials.

inputs.name: lifecycle
inputs.note: Lifecycle stage (active, nrnd, eol, obsolete or any stage a policy names); absent is the warning lifecycle(unknown).

inputs.name: eol_day
inputs.note: Estimated end-of-life date; within the policy horizon it is a warning.

inputs.name: ltb_day
inputs.note: Last-time-buy date; within the horizon it warns, once passed it blocks.

inputs.name: sourced_from
inputs.note: One supplier of the part; fewer distinct suppliers than min_sources is a warning.

inputs.name: cross
inputs.note: A form-fit-function alternate for the part, offered by part_alternate.

inputs.name: requires
inputs.note: A flag every part must carry with the value compliant, true, yes or qualified; otherwise missing(Flag) blocks.

inputs.name: min_sources
inputs.note: Fewest distinct suppliers a part may have before it warns.

inputs.name: eol_horizon_days
inputs.note: An end-of-life or last-time-buy date within this many days of today is due.

inputs.name: blocks_lifecycle
inputs.note: A lifecycle stage that blocks; when the policy names none, obsolete blocks.

inputs.name: warns_lifecycle
inputs.note: A lifecycle stage that warns; when the policy names none, nrnd and eol warn.

inputs.name: absolute_days
inputs.note: Today as a day count from 1970-01-01, the shared convention. Preferred over date.

inputs.name: date
inputs.note: Today as an ISO date, a YYYYMMDD integer or a day count, when absolute_days is absent.
